title: USB HID: Parse bit fields with correct bit order
description:
Implement little endian support for tvb_get_bits family of functions.
The big/little endian refers to bit numbering within an octet. In big
endian, the most significant bit is considered bit 0, while in little
endian the least significant bit is considered bit 0.

Add encoding parameters to proto tree bits format family functions.
Specify ENC_BIG_ENDIAN in all dissectors using these functions except in
USB HID that requires ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN to work correctly.

When formatting bits values, always display most significant bit on the
leftmost position regardless of the encoding. This results in no gaps
between octets and makes the displayed value comprehensible.

Close #4478
Fix #17014

notes.body: This is marked as draft because the `decode_bits_in_field()` needs to be made aware of the encoding as well. However, as this is pretty important change, it would be nice to get this looked at before the pretty formatting is done.
`decode_bits_in_field()` turned out to be pretty simple, as the representation that makes most sense simply requires calculating the number of leading dots.

Thanks for taking up this. I don't see any issues.

I'm surprised no other protocol needed LE bit order.  I expected you to find other places this was handled wrong when updating them.  Or may be they all implemented the in-place swap approach.

> I'm surprised no other protocol needed LE bit order. I expected you to find other places this was handled wrong when updating them. Or may be they all implemented the in-place swap approach.

There might be some uncovered bugs. I just put `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` in all other dissectors to not change their behavior.

I built this and tried a few of my captures.

I see this fixed at least one Keyboard's modifier keys being incorrectly identified.

On this one, I see the bits are double-counted in Padding.  Take a look at Frame 141 in  the attached capture.  The first byte in the HID Data after Report ID:

[MultiTouch_1-10_fingers.pcapng](/uploads/5c709f28f2c6a1761f427a269d103107/MultiTouch_1-10_fingers.pcapng)

I am not sure what you mean by double-counted bits, but the incorrect padding value is because `hf_usbhid_padding` type is `FT_BYTES` and `tvb_get_bits_array()` called inside `proto_tree_add_bits_item()` is silently assuming `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` (`tvb_get_bits_array()` does not take encoding parameter).

> I am not sure what you mean by double-counted bits, but the incorrect padding value...

It's the incorrect padding value.  I said double-counted because the same bits were set in both the 1-bit fields and again in the padding.

> It's the incorrect padding value. I said double-counted because the same bits were set in both the 1-bit fields and again in the padding.

I have implemented encoding support in `tvb_get_bits_array()` and the padding should be ok now.
Yes.  I built and agree the padding is OK now.

>no other protocol needed LE bit order

For example MAC address is little endian bitness. Yet in practice, you cannot see it, except if you actually insert an analyser right into the wire.

> For example MAC address is little endian bitness. Yet in practice, you cannot see it, except if you actually insert an analyser right into the wire.

The transmission bit order is pretty much completely irrelevant here. In USB the bits are transmitted LSB first and it is up to the capture engine (usbmon, USBPcap, OpenVizsla) to generate capture file with correct bytes (not bit reversed).

This change deals with unaligned bitfields that span across multiple bytes. @johnthacker comment at https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/4478#note_468195478 describes what this is all about (retrieving bits in different order as opposed to changing bits significance).

I believe that there are a few other protocols that could use this but deal with the issue with the `split_bits_item` formulation.

Split bits was difficult to use with USB HID because of the dynamic nature of the fields instead of having fixed position.

I reckon some of the other dissectors could be changed to use this as it's clearer and simpler, but it's obviously not necessary.

The code looks good to me. I've built it and checked with the capture attached to the OP in #17014, and the results seem correct now (except for a strange extra bit of "Usage: Generic Indicator" in frames 151, 153, and 165, but it's also there with a8f822bb8edae4193b1896a8c923a75afae8eaa7 reverted).

> except for a strange extra bit of "Usage: Generic Indicator" in frames 151, 153, and 165

The "Usage: Generic Indicator" is because in the HID Report descriptor in frame 76 there is the LED Page (0x08) Generic Indicator (0x4b) right after the modifier keys array.

I see, but why only one bit? There's Report Count (8) and Report Size (1), which are global items and should apply to this input too. And then there should be no padding, since all 8 bits are consumed by this LED input.

Why would all 8 bits be consumed by the LED input? Report Size is 1, so each usage inside this Input (Data, Var, Abs) consumes 1 bit. There is only one usage defined (Generic Indicator), so the rest (7 bits) is padding. While the padding might look like a byte in the tree, it is in fact 7 bits (FT_BYTES displays as hex string regardless of the number of bits, but this is out-of-scope of this merge request).
Ah, I see. No usage implies it's padding. OK, this looks correct.
